_comment: MODSET name->factor table for the production general-interval hook (frida/trampoline_inject.py, TTRMOD_MODE=modset). ONE install of the Python MetaInterval.start wrapper reads each started interval's getName() and setPlayRate's it with the factor of the FIRST matching entry -- so all cosmetic animation groups speed up at once, and nothing else is touched. factor = speed multiplier (3.0 = 3x faster / ~1/3 the duration). match = substring of the interval name (set prefix:true to anchor at the start instead). Entries are tried IN ORDER; put specific matches before broad ones. enabled:false stubs an entry out. Names matching NO entry are logged (log_unmatched) but never scaled, so gameplay-timing intervals stay intact. The interval NAMES are TTR's real ones (observed live via TTRMOD_LOGNAMES); the class is pinned per-build in trampoline_inject.py (META_INTERVAL_MODULE/CLASS) -- re-derive on an engine auto-patch.
_comment_context: The `context` section scales intervals by CREATION CONTEXT (a wrapped method sets a global flag; intervals that START during it are scaled), for a spawner that builds+starts its interval SYNCHRONOUSLY inside a wrappable, signature-resolvable method. Each entry names a readable METHOD; its owning class is resolved by that method's SIGNATURE (never the hashed class name), and the method is wrapped wrap-AROUND: the flag is set BEFORE the original runs and restored AFTER (in a finally, so it clears even if the original raises; nesting-safe). NB the street-tunnel walk is NOT such a case -- see the two disabled tunnelOut/tunnelIn entries: those readable methods only send a server b_set and the animation happens later in a HASHED handler, outside their window. The walk is handled by `spawn_context` (co_name) below. This section is kept for genuinely-synchronous spawners (and as approach-3 fallback: put a HASHED handler's own name here to resolve its class by that name's signature and wrap it wrap-around). method = readable method whose call brackets the interval creation; factor/group as for entries; enabled:false skips it.

Wrapping tunnelOut wrap-AROUND scales NOTHING: the open-toontown reference (toontown/toon/LocalToon.py) proves tunnelOut only calls self.b_setTunnelOut(...) -- a SERVER BROADCAST -- and does NOT animate. _comment_spawn_context: The `spawn_context` section scales an interval by the co_name of the Python FRAME THAT CALLED start() -- i.e. the (usually hashed) name of the method that spawned it. This is the fix for the street-tunnel WALK: the reference open-toontown LocalToon.handleTunnelIn/handleTunnelOut build an UNNAMED `self.tunnelTrack = Sequence(...)` (auto-named 'vlt8e0d5a85-<n>' on TTR, unmatchable by name) and immediately `.start()` it. Since start()'s wrapper is a native C trampoline (pushes no Python frame), tstate->frame at scale-time IS that handler frame; reading tstate->frame->f_code->co_name (PyThreadState.frame +0x18 -> PyFrameObject.f_code +0x20 -> PyCodeObject.co_name +0x70, CPython 3.8 ABI, offline-verified) yields the spawning function's name. An interval whose spawning co_name EXACTLY equals an entry's `co_name` is setPlayRate'd by that entry's factor -- exact match, so ONLY intervals spawned by a named function are touched and a hashed co_name (unique to its source) collides with nothing. co_name = the (hashed) spawning-method name; factor/group as for entries; enabled:false skips one. DISCOVERY: handleTunnelOut/handleTunnelIn are HASHED on TTR, so their real co_names are unknown until observed. Run one live tunnel walk with logging on -- every unmatched interval's DISTINCT spawning co_name is printed as [SPAWNCO] <co_name>; a NEW co_name appears exactly when you walk a tunnel (that is the hashed handler). Paste it into an entry's `co_name`. Best case (co_names not obfuscated) the readable guesses below already match on the first walk.

spawn_context._note: DEPARTURE walk. Best-effort readable guess: if TTR left this code object's co_name intact it scales on the first walk. If handleTunnelOut is hashed (likely -- STATUS: hashed on LocalToon), this won't match until you replace it with the hashed co_name from the [SPAWNCO] log of a single live tunnel walk. The interval it spawns is the unnamed self.tunnelTrack Sequence (auto-named vlt8e0d5a85-<n>).

ARRIVAL walk. Same as handleTunnelOut -- readable guess; replace with the hashed co_name discovered via [SPAWNCO] on a live tunnel walk if this doesn't match. Both directions are covered so that once the two hashed co_names are filled in, entering AND exiting a street tunnel both speed up.
